html:
Pashupatinath is a temple of the Hindu god Shiva on the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, Nepal, and the country's holiest Hindu shrine. A temple stood here by the time of the Licchavi kings, and the present building dates from the 1690s.

Shiva is worshipped here as Pashupati, lord of animals and protector of Nepal. Hindus from Nepal and India come in great numbers, above all at the festival of Maha Shivaratri. Only Hindus may enter the main courtyard.

On the river banks below are the cremation ghats where many Nepalis are burned. Kings of the Shah dynasty ruled as protectors of Hinduism, and the temple's priests by custom come from south India. It is part of the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage Site.
